question.problem:
The velocity of a car that starts moving, in meters per second, is given by the function $v(t),$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. The values of $v(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| $t$ | $0$ | $5$ | $10$ | $15$ | $20$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $v(t)$ | $0$ | $10$ | $25$ | $45$ | $70$ |

Approximate the acceleration ${v}^{′}(t)$ when $t=20$ using a backward difference approximation.
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{v}^{′}(t)≈\frac{v(t)-v(t-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the time $t=20.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{′}(20) & ≈\frac{v(20)-v(20-5)}{5} \\  & =\frac{v(20)-v(15)}{5} \\  & =\frac{70-45}{5} \\  & =\frac{25}{5} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

So the acceleration is $5\,\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2}.$
